top_categories.workout_context: 61ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
Race-pace efforts that mimic GFNY Punta del Este's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before March.

Road-specific control matters at GFNY Punta del Este. Practice on coastal start, steep inland hills, and a rolling: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 90 miles.
At mile 60 of 90, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
At GFNY Punta del Este, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of GFNY Punta del Este. Train it until it feels boring.
5,577ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
5,577ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at GFNY Punta del Este. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.

Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on coastal start, steep inland hills, and a rolling can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 90 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 5,577ft of climbing on coastal start, steep inland hills, and a rolling does to your power file on race day.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for GFNY Punta del Este’s 90 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at GFNY Punta del Este rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on coastal start, steep inland hills, and a rolling return to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on TT Threshold, Race Simulation, and Road Specific to prepare you for 90 miles of coastal start, steep inland hills, and a rolling return in Punta del Este, Maldonado Department, Uruguay.
